# Parkinson's disease — non-motor symptoms

> 6 concept packs from the research run on non-motor symptoms (neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech); 50 of the family's 1,155 claims are grouped under this section in llms-facts.txt. Educational research reference, not medical advice.
> Source: research run parkinsons-nonmotor-symptom-management · Generated: 2026-11-27 by llms-deep-optimizer v1.2.1 · Mode: family

## Concept packs

- [Run-level pack: Non-motor symptoms](https://llmsx.org/tree/parkinson-s-disease-non-motor-symptoms-neuropsychiatric-symptoms-sleep-disorders-autonomic-dysfunction-pain-and-fatigue-cognitive-impairment-swallowing-and-speech/): Run-level pack covering neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep disorders, autonomic dysfunction, pain and fatigue, cognitive impairment, swallowing and speech
- [PD autonomic dysfunction: orthostatic hypotension, constipation, bladder](https://llmsx.org/tree/pd-autonomic-dysfunction-orthostatic-hypotension-constipation-bladder/): Constipation can involve slow transit and impaired evacuation; macrogol and lubiprostone have trial support
- [PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment](https://llmsx.org/tree/pd-cognitive-impairment-and-dementia-treatment/): PD cognitive treatment depends on whether functional independence is preserved or cognition impairs daily activities
- [PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems](https://llmsx.org/tree/pd-dysphagia-sialorrhea-speech-and-voice-problems/): EMST has short-term swallowing trial evidence, but comparative and long-term dysphagia treatment evidence remains limited
- [PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy](https://llmsx.org/tree/pd-neuropsychiatric-symptoms-psychosis-depression-anxiety-apathy/): The cited sources treat PD psychosis, depression, anxiety and apathy as distinct problems with distinct assessment and treatment choices
- [PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms](https://llmsx.org/tree/pd-pain-fatigue-and-sensory-symptoms/): Treatment evidence is uneven: historical MDS ratings are qualified, PANDA and OXYDOPA did not establish their primary analgesic benefits
- [PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness](https://llmsx.org/tree/pd-sleep-disorders-rbd-insomnia-and-daytime-sleepiness/): Insomnia assessment considers other sleep disorders, and CBT-I evidence in PD is promising but limited by small studies and adherence

## Top sources, live-checked 2026-11-27

- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382 (23 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/): Modafinil evidence in PD is mixed: MDS 2019 calls it possibly useful while retaining insufficient efficacy evidence
- [nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71 (16 claims in this run)](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations): NICE advises considering augmentative and alternative communication equipment as Parkinson’s disease progresses and communication needs change
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078 (11 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/): The 2024 German guideline advises against using food supplements or herbal therapeutics to treat cognitive deficits in PD-MCI or PD dementia
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655 (6 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592655/): The 2020 review recommends slow position changes, avoiding heat and large carbohydrate-rich meals, and stepwise nonpharmacological treatment
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384 (5 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/): The 2023 AASM guideline conditionally supports transdermal rivastigmine for PD-associated RBD, based on one randomized trial
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530 (5 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/): PD COMM found no evidence of voice-handicap benefit for the trial’s NHS speech and language therapy arm versus no therapy
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389 (4 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2995389/): Evidence appraisal differs by level: Troche’s trial reported improved swallowing safety after EMST
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5039223 (4 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5039223/): For refractory detrusor overactivity, the urogenital review describes intradetrusor botulinum toxin as an option but explicitly warns about urinary retention
